notes: Typing / opens a list of commands, like the terminal. It shows the Claude Code commands worth having (compact, context, recap, init, code-review and more, only the ones your Claude Code has), Pocket's own actions (side chat, branch, new conversation, model, effort and plan usage) and your skills, grouped and narrowed as you type. On a computer use the arrow keys, then Enter or Tab; on a phone, tap. A command that needs nothing more runs as soon as you pick it. New conversation has the list too. The answer to a command such as /context or /usage now stays in the conversation after a reload, and a skill you ran reads back as you typed it rather than as the skill's own instructions. Requested by Brad.

Vault fixes from a new kind of bug review, where one agent describes how the Vault should behave without seeing its tests and another tests that description without seeing the code. A command run with a secret can no longer leave a helper process behind that ignored the request to stop and kept the secret. A username and password sent as an HTTP Basic login header, and a secret carried inside any longer base64 text, are now hidden in a command's output. An approval you give near the end of its 15 minutes stays good for 15 minutes after you answer instead of vanishing a minute later. A wrong passphrase is always refused and counted, even when the Vault's activity log cannot be written. And agents are pointed at the Vault skill correctly when Pocket is installed in a folder whose name has a space. Prompted by Casey's description of how he finds bugs.

Answer from the banner. When one action waits for your OK, the banner under the conversation header says what it is in plain words, shows the command or file, and carries Allow and Don't allow, so one tap decides it. One question with a few options shows the options as buttons the same way. Details or Answer still open the full sheet, and the sheet now closes itself once nothing is left waiting, instead of asking you to close it. Requested by Brad after talking with Casey.

Subagents in view, and their requests reach you. The Subagents row under the conversation controls now also reports work left running in the background, and each agent has Show activity, which follows the agent's own transcript while it works. A permission request or question from a subagent is shown with the agent's name, including one that arrives after the reply that started it has ended; before, those were dropped and the agent, and the conversation, waited for an answer that could not come. Codex subagents' requests are passed on too. Requested by Brad after talking with Casey.

Assistant mode has a Features section in Settings. Switch Projects, Files, Tasks, Inbox Watch and the Vault on or off there, and Automatic model choice. When Assistant mode is locked, it says which are on and to ask the person who runs Pocket to change them, and a library that is off says the same instead of sending you to Settings.

Fixes found while writing the manual. A message sent with After this reply keeps the model, effort and Codex mode you picked. A start link opens New conversation in its own folder. Steer now falls back to After this reply when the reply cannot take it. A finished Codex reply no longer buzzes your phone while you are watching it. On a computer, the plus on New conversation clears it. On a Mac, Codex conversations survive a Pocket restart. Inbox Watch sets itself up even after another job has posted to the Inbox, keeps its Start a conversation button, and notices when Gmail is connected to a different account. The Vault counts only wrong unlock attempts, and the Files share link stays the same when an agent looks it up.

Pocket Code has a manual: one page per feature (conversations, approvals, Projects, Files, Tasks, Inbox Watch, the Vault, voice, Settings and more) saying what it does, how to turn it on, how to use it and what to do when it misbehaves. It is written for you and for your agents: every agent Pocket starts is told where it is, and each Pocket skill names its page, so asking an agent how something in Pocket works gets an answer from the manual instead of a read through the code. It lives in docs/manual in the Pocket Code directory.

Inbox Watch reads back only memory that is about the email. The memory search always brought three past sessions or notes with each email, related or not, so an email about one customer's billing came with a session about another's. Now an item has to share the email's names, numbers or subject words, which cuts what each decision reads by about a third. The tidy pass also keeps an entry on your list while part of what it asked for has no one on it. Requested by Brad.

Typing / in a Codex conversation now offers /btw too, and picking it types /btw, ready for your question. Before, it was only suggested in Claude conversations, though typing it in full already worked in both.
